A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching methods, equations, empirical results and appendices. Figure 11 in v3 clips its axis and caption on the displayed page, but their embedded text is recoverable and supports comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, match/mismatch surprisal trajectories, co-occurrence analyses and causal attention-head interventions on CHILDES and Visual Dialog.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds per-instance VLM surprisal results and correlations between aggregate-head counts and grounding information gain.

M1.justification: Both versions use separate ENV/LAN token identities, causal language-model training, frozen DINOv2 visual representations, saliency and tuned-lens analyses, and head-zeroing interventions. No algorithmic or architectural modification is established.

E1.justification: CHILDES, caption-grounded Visual Dialog, image-grounded Visual Dialog and the LLaVA case study remain, with unchanged target vocabularies. Caption-grounded material moves to Appendix C.1, Table 3 and Figure 8; the added analyses use existing coverage.

E2.justification: The Transformer, Mamba-2 and unidirectional LSTM comparisons remain unchanged, as do the layer-matched random-head intervention controls. Newly cited symbol-binding studies are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use the same templates, target lists, model configurations, checkpoint schedules and intervention thresholds. v3 clarifies that templates are inference-only. Removed hyperparameter documentation does not establish changed settings, and the new plots analyze existing evaluations.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a per-context VLM surprisal breakdown in Figure 11 and examines whether words with more aggregate heads have greater grounding gain in Figure 13. These are focused supplementary analyses within the existing experimental settings.

E5.justification: v3 retains the five-seed reporting and p < 0.001 intervention significance convention, but removes the explicit seed values 42, 142, 242, 342 and 442 from v1 Appendix B.2. This reduces seed disclosure without establishing fewer runs.

E6.justification: Figure 13 adds head-count/gain R² values of 0.847 for CHILDES and 0.250 and 0.175 for VLM thresholds of 70% and 90%. Figure 11 adds per-instance VLM surprisals. The retained intervention results in Table 2 and Figure 7 are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions of surprisal, grounding information gain, its expected log-likelihood-ratio interpretation and attention saliency remain unchanged. Neither version develops additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly frames CHILDES as a synthetic proxy for hypotheses about multimodal grounding and adds a symbol-binding contribution in Section 6. This refines the contribution's scope while retaining the abstract's central claims about middle-layer aggregation and architectural differences.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly distinguishes symbol binding in the textual testbed from environmental grounding and adopts a more qualified philosophical interpretation of symbolic structure. The limitations concerning CLIP language priors, dispersed visual information and full-scale causal intervention remain.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1 Appendices B.2–B.3 and both training and CHILDES-processing repository links. This eliminates learning rates, schedules, hidden size, batch sizes, optimizer settings, hardware and training-time information. Checkpoint lists remain, and inference-only template usage is clarified.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds positioning relative to binding research by Feng and Steinhardt, Dai et al., Feng et al. and Yang et al. It replaces the explicit challenge to Gubelmann with discussion of Pavlick's empirical stance. Most related-work coverage remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the synthetic-testbed-to-visual-validation narrative, relocate caption-grounded discussion to Appendix C.1 and reorganize appendix headings. Impact and LLM-use statements are added. The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns. Caption examples and plots are split into appendix displays, Figure 5a is transposed, and Figures 6–7 are rearranged. Figures 11 and 13 are added; Figure 11's horizontal axis and caption extend below the visible page.

improvement.justification: v3 improves conceptual framing and adds useful supplementary analyses, but removes substantial reproducibility information and repository links from v1 Appendix B. The clipped Figure 11 also impairs readability. With the central methods and causal results unchanged, these reporting losses outweigh the limited analytical and explanatory gains.
